title: South Carolina Code of Laws Title 8, Chapter 11, Article 7 - Annual Leave for State Employees
source_id: S.C. Code Ann. tit. 8, ch. 11, art. 7 (secs. 8-11-610 to 8-11-680)
verified_how: fetched the register's Title 8 chapter index (https://www.scstatehouse.gov/code/title8.php): title 'Title 8 - Public Officers and Employees', chapter row 'CHAPTER 11 - STATE OFFICERS AND EMPLOYEES' with no [REPEALED] marker (sibling 'CHAPTER 30 - RECORDING AND REPORTING IMMIGRATION LAW VIOLATIONS [REPEALED]' shows the marker is in use); then fetched https://www.scstatehouse.gov/code/t08c011.php, whose heading reads 'CHAPTER 11 / State Officers and Employees' and which contains 'ARTICLE 7 - Annual Leave for State Employees' running from SECTION 8-11-610 (Manner in which annual leave is computed) to SECTION 8-11-680 (Application of article). Currency: current through the 2025 Session.
notes: IMPORTANT SCOPE LIMIT: this binds the State as an employer, not private employers. South Carolina has no general private-sector annual-leave, sick-leave or holiday-pay entitlement statute; private-sector family and medical leave is federal (FMLA, 29 U.S.C. ch. 28). Two adjacent provisions a human should weigh as alternatives, both verified in force on the register's own indexes: Title 8, Chapter 11, Article 9 (State Employee Leave-Transfer Program), and Title 38, Chapter 103 - the Paid Family Leave Insurance Act, enacted by 2024 Act No. 206 (H.4832) sec. 2, effective 21 May 2024 (HISTORY lines on https://www.scstatehouse.gov/code/t38c103.php), which authorises insurers to write paid family leave insurance as an insurance product but creates no employee leave entitlement, which is why it was not chosen here.
